questions.q: What does `new GlideRecord('incident')` do by itself, with no further calls?
options: Creates a cursor object pointed at the incident table's schema, without fetching any rows yet
Immediately loads every incident record into memory
Immediately deletes the incident table if it is empty
Throws an error unless a sys_id is passed to the constructor
questions.explain: Creating a GlideRecord doesn't query anything by itself — no database call happens until you call `.get()` or `.query()`.

options: Looks up the incident with that sys_id, and if found, logs its number
Creates a new incident with that sys_id
Deletes the incident with that sys_id
Logs an error because `.get()` requires two arguments
questions.explain: `.get()` retrieves a single record (by sys_id here) and returns true/false depending on whether a match was found.

questions.q: Inside a Business Rule, what is `current`?
options: A GlideRecord object, already queried and positioned on the record that triggered the rule
A plain JavaScript object with no connection to GlideRecord
A string containing the sys_id of the triggering record
A function you must call to create your own GlideRecord
questions.explain: `current` is handed to the Business Rule already positioned as a GlideRecord — you don't need to query for it yourself.

questions.q: Which statement best describes why GlideRecord matters so much in ServiceNow server scripting?
options: Business Rules, Script Includes, and Scheduled Jobs all rely on GlideRecord in some form to touch table data
GlideRecord is only used in Client Scripts, never on the server
GlideRecord is an optional convenience API with several equally common alternatives
GlideRecord only works on the incident table
questions.explain: GlideRecord is the foundation most server-side scripting constructs are built on, across Business Rules, Script Includes, and Scheduled Jobs.

questions.q: If `gr.get('99999999999999999999999999999999')` is called with a sys_id that doesn't exist, what happens?
options: `.get()` returns false, and the cursor is not positioned on any record
ServiceNow throws an unrecoverable script error
A new blank record is automatically created with that sys_id
`.get()` returns the first record in the table instead
questions.explain: `.get()` returns false when no match is found — it never substitutes another record or throws for a missing sys_id.
